meta.title: Tax, Regulatory, Insurance & Transaction-Cost Environment
meta.why_it_matters: For a decision to SELL, transaction taxes and Proposition 13 reassessment are first-order. For a decision to HOLD, the property-tax cap and the tenant's NNN obligation to reimburse taxes are first-order. Both sides of the decision are governed by the same body of law, so this page is load-bearing rather than background.

rows.m: Proposition 13 — maximum base property tax rate
rows.p: California Constitution, Article XIII A (1978, current)
rows.s: Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector — property tax bill components
rows.n: The General Tax Levy is 1% of net taxable value. Voted indebtedness, direct assessments and special charges are added on top.

rows.m: Proposition 13 — cap on annual growth of assessed value
rows.v: Maximum 2% per year, or the California CPI increase if lower, so long as ownership does not change
rows.s: California State Board of Equalization — Proposition 13 / property tax resources

rows.m: Proposition 13 inflation factor actually applied in Los Angeles County
rows.v: The maximum allowable 2% factor was applied because the California Consumer Price Index exceeded the constitutional limit
rows.s: Los Angeles County Assessor — 2026 Assessment Roll
rows.n: Added approximately $43 billion to the county roll.

rows.m: Change in ownership — reassessment trigger
rows.v: A change in ownership establishes a new base-year value at full market value as of the date of transfer
rows.s: California State Board of Equalization — property tax rules
rows.n: CRITICAL TO THE SELL DECISION: a sale resets the buyer's assessed value to the price paid. If the current owner's Prop 13 base-year value is far below market, the buyer inherits a materially higher tax bill, and that higher bill is priced into what a buyer will pay. Under an NNN lease the same reassessment flows straight through to the tenant's tax-reimbursement obligation.

rows.m: Los Angeles County — total property tax rate for a specific parcel (Tax Rate Area)
rows.s: Los Angeles County Auditor-Controller — Tax Rate Area Lookup
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — the total rate is parcel-specific and requires the Tax Rate Area code from the Assessor record. The County divides property into hundreds of TRAs and the Board of Supervisors sets rates under Article XIII A of the State Constitution. Official lookup linked. FLAG F-04.

rows.m: Los Angeles County property tax — instalment due dates and delinquency
rows.v: First instalment due November 1, delinquent after December 10; second instalment due February 1, delinquent after April 10
rows.s: Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector
rows.n: Under an NNN lease these are the dates on which the tenant's reimbursement obligation crystallises. A tenant default here is a landlord exposure unless the lease provides for direct payment or reserves.

rows.m: Los Angeles County — documentary transfer tax rate
rows.s: Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder / County of Los Angeles
rows.n: LEFT BLANK. The county rate was consistently reported by secondary sources as $1.10 per $1,000 but was not read directly from an official lacounty.gov page in this session. Confirm at the official Registrar-Recorder / Treasurer and Tax Collector pages. FLAG F-23.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles — documentary transfer tax rate
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance — Real Property Transfer Tax and Measure ULA FAQ
rows.r: $4.50 per $1,000 of consideration (0.45%), equivalent to $2.25 per $500
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — not read directly from finance.lacity.gov in this session. FLAG F-23.

rows.m: Measure ULA (United to House Los Angeles) — statutory basis and effective date
rows.v: Los Angeles Municipal Code Section 21.9.2; approved by Los Angeles voters in November 2022; applicable to conveyances of real estate occurring on or after April 1, 2023
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department — United to House LA Tax Exemption Eligibility Guidelines / FAQ
rows.n: Read from the official LAHD FAQ PDF. The tax is collected at escrow by the Los Angeles County Recorder together with other local documentary transfer taxes; the City's portion is remitted to the City Office of Finance.

rows.m: Measure ULA — rates
rows.v: 4% on transactions valued above the lower threshold and below the upper threshold; 5.5% on transactions above the upper threshold
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department — official ULA FAQ
rows.n: The ordinance text describes the tax as being at the rate of 4% OF THE CONSIDERATION OR VALUE — that is, of the whole price, not of the excess above the threshold.

rows.m: Measure ULA — dollar thresholds originally enacted
rows.v: over $5 million and under $10 million for the 4% rate; over $10 million for the 5.5% rate
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department — official ULA FAQ

rows.m: Measure ULA — current indexed dollar thresholds
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance — Real Property Transfer Tax and Measure ULA FAQ
rows.r: $5,400,000 (lower) and $10,900,000 (upper), superseding $5,300,000 / $10,600,000 which applied July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
rows.n: LEFT BLANK AND FLAGGED. Thresholds are indexed annually to the Bureau of Labor Statistics Chained Consumer Price Index and are published each year before July 1 by the City Office of Finance. Multiple secondary sources report the same pair of figures, but the official Office of Finance FAQ was not read directly in this session. Verify before relying on them in a transaction. FLAG F-24.

rows.m: Measure ULA — measurement base relative to liens
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
rows.r: ULA is measured on consideration or value INCLUDING the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining at the time of sale, whereas the base City transfer tax is measured EXCLUSIVE of liens
rows.n: LEFT BLANK AND FLAGGED — reported by secondary sources only. This matters if a buyer assumes existing debt. FLAG F-24.

rows.m: Measure ULA — exemptions administered by the City Office of Finance
rows.v: (1) Nonprofits that received IRS 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status at least 10 years ago and carry assets of less than one billion dollars; (2) government entities, whether state, local or federal; (3) any purchaser exempt from the City's taxing power under the state or federal constitutions
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department — official ULA FAQ
rows.n: LAHD separately administers a technical-assistance exemption programme for qualified affordable-housing organisations, community land trusts and limited equity housing cooperatives that record an affordability covenant.

rows.m: Measure ULA — geographic scope
rows.v: Applies to real property transfers within the CITY of Los Angeles only
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Housing Department — official ULA FAQ
rows.n: MATERIAL TO THE DECISION: if the subject parcel sits in the City of Los Angeles and trades above the ULA threshold, a sale carries a 4% or 5.5% tax on the ENTIRE price. If it sits in an adjacent jurisdiction (Beverly Hills, West Hollywood, Vernon, Culver City, Santa Monica or unincorporated county land), ULA does not apply. This is a binary, order-of-magnitude swing in net sale proceeds.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles minimum wage — current rate
rows.v: $18.42 per hour, all employers regardless of size
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards — official Minimum Wage Ordinance notice
rows.n: Adjusted annually under Los Angeles Minimum Wage Ordinance Section 187.02. LAMC Sections 187 and 188.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles minimum wage — applicability test
rows.v: Applies to employees who work at least two hours in a week within the geographic boundaries of the City of Los Angeles
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards
rows.n: Enforced by the Bureau of Contract Administration, Office of Wage Standards, which may investigate violations, inspect workplaces, interview employees and review payroll records. LAMC Section 188.04 protects employees from retaliation.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles paid sick leave
rows.v: Required of all employers under the Los Angeles Minimum Wage Ordinance
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards — official notice
rows.n: Payroll records must be retained for four years.

rows.m: California — statewide minimum wage for 2026
rows.s: California Department of Industrial Relations
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — not read directly from dir.ca.gov in this session. FLAG F-09.

rows.m: Jack in the Box Inc. — California operating cost exposure disclosed in its own filings
rows.v: The company cited 'a reversal of additional FUTA taxes in California' as a partial offset to commodity inflation in its restaurant-level margin
rows.s: Jack in the Box Inc., Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 (fourth quarter fiscal 2025 earnings release), filed with the SEC
rows.n: Official evidence that California payroll taxes are large enough to move a national operator's disclosed margin. Reinforces why the LA wage floor at R-16 matters to tenant solvency.

rows.m: Los Angeles County — Assessor parcel-level record for the subject property
rows.s: Los Angeles County Assessor — Parcel Access
rows.n: Withheld under the privacy protocol. The official public lookup is linked for manual review. FLAG F-01.

rows.m: City of Los Angeles business tax obligations of the tenant operator
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance — Business Tax
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — no tenant operating record supplied and no official rate table was read line by line in this session. Under a NNN lease this is the tenant's obligation, but tenant insolvency converts it into a landlord re-tenanting problem. FLAG F-25.

rows.m: Owner-level tax treatment of a sale (federal and California capital gain, depreciation recapture)
rows.s: Internal Revenue Service; California Franchise Tax Board
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — requires the owner's basis, holding period and entity structure, all of which are personal financial information withheld under the privacy protocol. Not a legal or tax opinion. FLAG F-01.

rows.m: Section 1031 like-kind exchange availability and deadlines
rows.s: Internal Revenue Service — Like-Kind Exchanges
rows.n: LEFT BLANK — no election has been made and no qualified intermediary engagement exists. Recorded here only as an option to evaluate, not as an assumption. FLAG F-26.

rows.m: California wildfire disclosure requirements affecting insurers
rows.s: California Department of Insurance
rows.r: New wildfire disclosure laws took effect January 1, 2025 requiring insurers to give clearer information on coverage limits and non-renewal reasons in high-risk areas; a 12-month moratorium on non-renewals was extended from January 1, 2026 to commercial properties, HOAs, condos and non-profits
rows.n: LEFT BLANK AND FLAGGED — read from secondary summaries only. Materially relevant because the tenant must carry property insurance under an NNN lease. FLAG F-27.

rows.m: Los Angeles crime statistics relevant to trade-area demand
rows.s: Los Angeles Police Department — COMPSTAT weekly snapshots; LA City open data portal
rows.r: LAPD COMPSTAT snapshots report citywide year-to-date Part I crime declining roughly 6.8% in 2025 versus 2024
rows.n: LEFT BLANK AND FLAGGED. The official LAPD COMPSTAT PDFs are published as multi-column scanned tables; the extraction of specific citywide totals in this session was not unambiguous, so no figure is published.
